## Software for quality assessment

In this part of the module, we'll look at software applications that can be used to assess the quality of data from ONT sequencing runs. We'll be focussing on two pieces of software: FastQC and NanoPlot.

- FastQC (you've already seen this): generic tool for assessing the quality of next generation sequencing data.
- NanoPlot: quality assessment software specifically built for ONT data.

## NanoPlot

Let's use the NanoPlot software to assess the quality of our unaligned `.bam` data.  We can run NanoPlot 
interactively (i.e., we don't need to submit it as a slurm job), and it wil produce an HTML-based report 
that can be viewed in a browser.

Specify a `.bam` file to run NanoPlot on (**PLEASE:** use **TAB COMPLETE** to move down through the directories):

~~~
BAMFILE=bam-unaligned/NO_MISSV2_P2I/P2I_96/20260413_1636_P2I-00014-B_PBK98658_853a956f/bam_pass/barcode01/PBK98658_pass_barcode01_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam 
~~~
{: .bash}

### Running Nanoplot 

Load the NanoPlot module:

~~~
module load NanoPlot
~~~
{: .bash}

Run NanoPlot on a single `.bam` file:

~~~
NanoPlot -o nanoplot_fastmodel/barcode01 \
         -p bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_ \
         --ubam $BAMFILE
~~~
{: .bash}

Command syntax:

- `NanoPlot`: run the NanoPlot command (note that the capital N and P are required).
- `-o nnanoplot_fastmodel/barcode01`: folder for output (`-o`) to be written.
- `-p bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_`: prefix (`-p`) to be appended to start of each filename in the output folder.      
- `--ubam $BAMFILE`: the unaligned bam (`ubam`) file to process with NanoPlot.

Let's check what output was generated:

~~~
ls -1 nanoplot_fastmodel/barcode01
~~~
{: .bash}

~~~
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_LengthvsQualityScatterPlot_dot.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_LengthvsQualityScatterPlot_dot.png
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_LengthvsQualityScatterPlot_kde.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_LengthvsQualityScatterPlot_kde.png
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_NanoPlot_20261113_1235.log
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_NanoPlot-report.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_NanoStats.txt
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_Non_weightedHistogramReadlength.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_Non_weightedHistogramReadlength.png
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_Non_weightedLogTransformed_HistogramReadlength.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_Non_weightedLogTransformed_HistogramReadlength.png
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_WeightedHistogramReadlength.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_WeightedHistogramReadlength.png
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_WeightedLogTransformed_HistogramReadlength.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_WeightedLogTransformed_HistogramReadlength.png
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_Yield_By_Length.html
bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_Yield_By_Length.png
~~~
{: .output}

The file that we are interested in is the HTML report: `bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_NanoPlot-report.html`

To view this in your browser:

1. Use the file browser (left panel of Jupyter window) to navigate to the `nanoplot_fastmodel/barcode01` folder.
2. Control-click (Mac) or right-click (Windows/Linux) on the "bacteria_fastmodel_barcode01_NanoPlot-report.html" file and choose "Open in New Browser Tab".
3. The report should now be displayed in a new tab in your browser.

### Processing multiple `.bam` files

Nanoplot doesn't have a built-in mechanism for processing multiple `.bam` files and keeping the output separate for each.
If you give it multiple `.bam` files (e.g., via `Nanoplot --ubam *.bam`) it will combine all of the results into a 
single report.

In order to process each of the `.bam` files separately, you can use a loop:

~~~
FOLDER=bam-unaligned/NO_MISSV2_P2I/P2I_96/20260413_1636_P2I-00014-B_PBK98658_853a956f/bam_pass/

for i in barcode02  barcode03 unclassified 
do 
    NanoPlot -o nanoplot_fastmodel/$i \
             -p bacteria_fastmodel_$i_ \
             --ubam $FOLDER/$i/*.bam
done
~~~
{: .bash}

Once this has completed, we can check to see what has been created:

~~~
ls -1 nanoplot_fastmodel
~~~
{: .bash}

~~~
barcode01
barcode02
barcode03
unclassified
~~~
{: .output}

There is now one folder of Nanoplot output for each barcoded sample.


## FastQC

Load the FastQC module:

~~~
module load FastQC
~~~
{: .bash}

Make a folder for the FastQC output to written to:

~~~
mkdir fastqc_fastmodel
~~~
{: .bash}

Unlike Nanoplot, FastQC *can* handle multiple `.bam` files at once (so a command like his will work: `fastqc -t 4 -o fastqc_fastmodel $FOLDER/*/*.bam`).

BUT, because we've also got all of the `.bam` files from the other barcodes (and we don't want to run FastQC for these empty files), can can use 
the same approach as above.

Let's re-use the `$FOLDER` variable we created. 

Reminder:

~~~
tree $FOLDER
~~~
{: .bash}

~~~
bam-unaligned/NO_MISSV2_P2I/P2I_96/20260413_1636_P2I-00014-B_PBK98658_853a956f/bam_pass/
├── barcode01
│   ├── PBK98658_pass_barcode01_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam
│   └── PBK98658_pass_barcode01_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam.bai
├── barcode02
│   ├── PBK98658_pass_barcode02_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam
│   └── PBK98658_pass_barcode02_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam.bai
├── barcode03
│   ├── PBK98658_pass_barcode03_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam
│   └── PBK98658_pass_barcode03_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam.bai
.
.
.
└── unclassified
    ├── PBK98658_pass_unclassified_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam
    └── PBK98658_pass_unclassified_853a956f_57f83f46_0.bam.bai
~~~
{: .output}

Fun fact - Nanoplot created a `.bai` (bam index) file for us when it processed the data.

Run FastQC on our data:

~~~
for i in barcode01 barcode02  barcode03 unclassified
do 
    fastqc -t 4 -o fastqc_fastmodel $FOLDER/$i/*.bam
done
~~~
{: .bash}

Command syntax:

- `fastqc`: run the `fastqc` command
- `-t 4`: use four cpus to make it go faster (the `-t` is for "threads").
- `-o fastqc_fastmodel`: specify output folder.
- `$FOLDER/*/*.bam`: data files to analyse (all bam files in all directories under $FOLDER).

Check the output:

~~~
ls -1 fastqc_fastmodel
~~~
{: .bash}

~~~
PBK98658_pass_barcode01_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.html
PBK98658_pass_barcode01_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.zip
PBK98658_pass_barcode02_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.html
PBK98658_pass_barcode02_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.zip
PBK98658_pass_barcode03_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.html
PBK98658_pass_barcode03_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.zip
PBK98658_pass_unclassified_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.html
PBK98658_pass_unclassified_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.zip
~~~
{: .output}

As we did with the NanoPlot output, we can view the HTML report in the browser:

1. Use the file browser (left panel of Jupyter window) to navigate to the `fastqc_fastmodel` folder.
2. Control-click (Mac) or right-click (Windows/Linux) on the "PBK98658_pass_barcode01_853a956f_57f83f46_0_fastqc.html" 
file and choose "Open in New Browser Tab".
3. The report should now be displayed in a new tab in your browser.
